coverage_summary: Revisited official World Bank energy access, industrial-transition and distribution-system evidence, and the aviation operational resilience issue documented in today's approved Global Macro. Previous approvals and historical results do not demonstrate a new November 15 disbursement, commissioning or measured productivity effect. Aviation disruption is a structural-resilience hypothesis, not yet a quantified investable or canonical condition. No candidate met the evidence threshold.

sources_checked.name: World Bank Brazil Amazon energy access
World Bank Northeast Brazil energy transition and jobs
World Bank India electricity distribution outcomes

hypotheses_under_review.subject: Aviation network operational resilience
hypotheses_under_review.hypothesis: Centralized system interruption may raise the value of redundancy and recovery capability
hypotheses_under_review.observable_trigger: Primary FAA/DOT quantified recurrence, repair capital expenditure and implementation milestones
hypotheses_under_review.invalidation: No recurring operational impact or measurable cost avoided

review_limitations: Sources are dated baseline materials, not newly issued 15 November project milestones.
No independently verified new disbursement, commissioning, regulation in force, measured productivity gain or project economics.
